acceptance: docs/internal/tpc-measured-intervals.md exists. Every call site in benchbox/core/tpch, tpcds, tpcdi and throughput that starts or stops a measured interval through mono_time(), elapsed_seconds() or time.time() (not import lines or helper definitions) is covered by a row or listed with a reason in a short 'not a measured interval' section; the PR lists the grep commands used and the count of call sites against the count of rows.

Every row fills six columns: file and symbol (no bare line numbers), governing clause (spec name, version, number), what is inside, what is outside, deviation status ('none' or an existing tracker item id), and the known-deviations entry where one applies. The PR lists each distinct clause with the page of the spec PDF where it was read.

Every clause cited in the Description appears with a number the author verified by reading the spec; the TPC-DI timed and untimed clauses are numbered; the 5.3.7.2 paraphrase states both interval endpoints. The locality ADR item 6 and result-schema-2-4-producer-20261022 are cited. No spec PDF is committed and no clause is quoted beyond one sentence.
The known-deviations list matches the tracker: each item id named exists and is open or done, checked with show_item when the PR is opened.
docs/internal/throughput-result-alignment.md links to the page; make docs-validate passes; the page is absent from docs/publish-allowlist.txt.

description:
Problem. Which work sits inside each benchmark timer is decided by spec clauses, but no repo page cites them. The TPC-H RF1 cost analysis missed clause 5.3.7.10 for that reason, and four tracker items carry timer claims that the specs contradict or confirm without anyone having checked. The root cause recorded in the analysis is that the TPC timing clauses are not captured in the repo as cited, tested requirements.

Deliverable: docs/internal/tpc-measured-intervals.md (unpublished page; do not add it to docs/publish-allowlist.txt). One row per timer site in benchbox/core/tpch, tpcds, tpcdi and throughput that starts or stops a measured interval: TPC-H and TPC-DS per-query power timing, RF1 and RF2, the refresh stream window, throughput stream windows and Ts, TPC-DS data maintenance, TPC-DI load and ETL. Columns: file and symbol (no bare line numbers), governing clause (spec, version, number), what is inside the interval, what is outside, deviation status (none, or the tracker item that owns the fix). Link it from docs/internal/throughput-result-alignment.md (timing-window paragraph).

Recorded decision to reconcile and cite: the accepted locality ADR amendment 'Round Trip Removed and Platform Timings' (item 6: timers measure only the query; adapters move tag setup, stats lookups, validation, plan capture and power-test query generation out of the measured timer; runs record run.timing_method and are compared and ranked within one method). The ADR moved to the site repository in #3545; its pre-move text is docs/development/adr/adr-client-link-locality-disclosure.md at commit e4a8a09091^. The open item result-schema-2-4-producer-20261022 owns writing timing_method (the code reads it but no producer writes it). Cite both in the page.

Clauses to verify and cite (read each from the spec, then paraphrase; quote at most one sentence per clause):
- TPC-H 3.0.1 (https://www.tpc.org/tpc_documents_current_versions/pdf/tpc-h_v3.0.1.pdf): 2.5.3.1, 5.3.6.1 (Ts), 5.3.7.2 (a query interval runs from submission of the query to submission of the next query, or for the last query to the last output character received by the driver; list BenchBox's interval endpoint as a deviation if it differs), 5.3.7.3 (RF interval: first character submitted until last transaction committed), 5.3.7.10 (before the refresh stream the dbgen data may only be generated, permuted and relocated; formatting and database activity are timed).
- TPC-DS 4.0.0 (https://www.tpc.org/tpc_documents_current_versions/pdf/tpc-ds_v4.0.0.pdf): 5.2.3 (dsdgen execution not timed), 5.2.5 and 5.2.7 (loading the refresh data, including into a staging area, is timed), 7.4.9.1 (maintenance interval start).
- TPC-DI 1.1.0 (https://www.tpc.org/tpc_documents_current_versions/pdf/tpc-di_v1.1.0.pdf): find and cite the clause numbers for what is timed (transformation begins with the SUT reading Source Data) and what is untimed (data generation, copy to staging). No clause number for TPC-DI was verified when this item was written.

Known deviations to list, each linked to its item: power-test-times-query-generation-20261031; result-schema-2-4-producer-20261022 (row-count validation and metadata propagation inside the power per-query timer); derived-power-export-rounding-20261017; perf-tpch-rf1-bulk-load-20261031 (cost, not a deviation); tpch-refresh-precheck-timing-decision-20261103 (three sites, including the standalone maintenance test); tpch-refresh-stream-window-excludes-connect-20261103; tpcds-maintenance-timer-hygiene-20261103; tpcds-maintenance-data-source-decision-20261103 and tpcds-maintenance-dsdgen-refresh-data-20261103; fetch-timing-contract-decision-20261103. Also check, and list if confirmed, whether TPC-DS throughput query generation runs inside the timer when enable_preflight is False (benchbox/core/tpcds/throughput_test.py). List the deviations recorded in the tracker item tpch-refresh-functions-in-power-and-throughput (duration rounding, 1000x clamp, Ts rounding, two-run rule) by reading it.

Guardrails for all code work: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create); never edit the primary clone. No explanatory comments or docstrings in source (make comment-policy-check). Durations use benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()/elapsed_seconds(). Add a changelog.d/ fragment. Cited line numbers are orientation only: re-read the named symbols, docs and spec clauses before editing and treat a mismatch as a reason to stop and update this item. No live-cloud runs without owner approval; heavy runs only through make heavy-run or a lock-taking entry point. Green focused tests are not release certification.
